title: Owner: stated / assumed / unclear, one keyword per line
body:
Journal #6: the small model reports what the message says with `stated`, what it adds with `assumed`, and an unintelligible or request-free message with `unclear`. One keyword per line.

Rationale as it stands in AGENTS.md direction 5: asserted statements are turn-local evidence, while suppositions, reported speech and model assumptions are used only conditionally or reported; none is a sourced fact.

author: owner
title: Owner decisions Q-DATA-1..4: every question type is formalizable
body:
Journal #28 (recorded by an agent, state `decision`): every question type must be formalizable (no unformalized case); documenting what and how we formalize matters, the reasoning outcome does not.

- **Q1:** an explicit universal mode in `query`.
- **Q2:** time as an unknown (`role time ?t`, `select ?t`).
- **Q3:** keep the current causal convention (a clause becomes its own proposition; "because of X" is a role).
- **Q4:** `assumed` stays optional and may state the queried proposition; teach the model to use `assumed` for vague, multi-interpretation messages, without over-generating such cases.

Trigger: the pilot showed 23 of 27 `assumed` wires restating the queried proposition (journal #27).

body:
Journal #33 (recorded by an agent, state `decision`). This extends the earlier rule that `unclear` has only two kinds.

- **Ambiguity (Q-ARCH-1):** `assumed` disambiguation by default; `unclear kind ambiguous` with repeatable `reading` lines (2–4) for a minority of messages with a visible ambiguity and no preferable reading.
- **Noise (Q-ARCH-4):** keyboard-adjacent errors (QWERTY, Romanian standard and programmer layouts), transposition, omission, insertion, doubling, space split/merge, diacritics, phonetic and autocorrect errors; `stated` values are quoted as written.

Implemented the same day (journal #44, DS021).

author: owner
title: Owner decisions Q-LANG-1..7 and Q-DATA-7: words, not operators; the model does not decide
body:
Journals #75 (owner-via-orchestrator) and #76. Principle: every construct as close to natural language as possible (no parentheses, no operator symbols); the small LLM does not think or decide, it proposes the best literal approximation and the reasoner deals with the rest.

- **Q-LANG-1:** NL-close comparative, superlative and value forms (compare/rank words, value variables).
- **Q-LANG-2:** quantifier words on `mode every` (all, none, not_all, most, half, at_least N).
- **Q-LANG-3:** two time variables with an NL ordering keyword (order before/after).
- **Q-LANG-4:** no new unclear kind; the simplest literal fragment query (`fragment follow_up`, completed by the host from context).
- **Q-LANG-5:** first person formalized with canonical "the user" forms.
- **Q-LANG-6:** a modal stays in the relation phrase; advice is `not_computable`.
- **Q-LANG-7:** alternatives via an any-group or one yes/no query per option; integer arithmetic via a words-only `constraint` (division `not_computable`).
- **Q-DATA-7:** NC or unlicensed datasets are used for statistics only (DS014).

The same decision put training phase B on hold until the expanded data was final.

Why: the independent pilot showed 71% of real messages needed a construct DS021 lacked (data-expansion proposal).

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: mt-training-agent
title: SOP Lang through a translation tokenizer: newlines and indentation need a line encoding
body:
Measured on all 28,948 formalizer-v1 train+dev rows. Marian (opus-mt-ROMANCE-en, opus-mt-roa-en, opus-mt-tc-bible-big-roa-en) and mt5-small SentencePiece normalization erase newlines and two-space indentation, which SOP Lang needs (the parser rejects wire fields without two spaces).

- **Fix:** a reversible encoding (`training/python/seq2seq_text.py`): a line break plus 2*K spaces becomes the added token `<nK>` (K = 0..7).
- **Result:** with it, every target round-trips exactly through all four tokenizers, and no target has an unknown token. `@`, `$`, `?`, straight quotes and Romanian diacritics are all represented.
- **Unknown tokens:** only 10 source messages have one, the curly quote U+201D.
- **Length:** SOP is about 2.1 Marian tokens per message token (median); the longest target is 3,099 tokens, beyond Marian's 512 positions.

author: Fable review
title: Clause decomposition: short wires chained with $ (proposal)
body:
**Proposal (PROPOSED, not normative):** `eval/reports/current/sop-clause-decomposition-proposal.md`.

**Diagnosis.** In distribution the flat language is not the bottleneck (conditional 97.5%, ordering 93%, causal 89%: memorized templates). On real text it is: on the 289 wild rows with a subordinating connective SmolLM2-135M's proposition F1 is 0.41 against 0.63 elsewhere; the worst wild gaps are G10 conditionals (0.09), G09 (0.22), G30 (0.24), G21 (0.27), G23 (0.28), G27 (0.29). The golds lose structure in three ways: a clause stuffed into a string value, a dropped link between two propositions (because/after/so), and an "if" clause made global for every question of the message.

**Recommended basis.** Clause analysis (EN/RO "analiza frazei") as the pedagogy; a closed PDTB-3/SDRT-derived relation set; a flat neo-Davidsonian representation where a proposition is a referable value (MRS handles; DS004's own event reification); QDMR-style `$` back-references for chaining; Split-and-Rephrase/DisSim as the data method; AMR as the cautionary tale.

**Language change (minimal).** (1) `clause TYPE $id` line on stated/assumed/query/match with seven types: cause, condition, concession, purpose, before, after, during. (2) `$id` as a role value: the event of a statement or the answers of an earlier query. Everything else unchanged. This revisits DS021's `proposition_not_ground` ban on `$` in stated/assumed; the consequences (parser, admission, guard, lowering, packet, Wire F1 keys, audit check, wire help, DS021/DS004/DS022 text) are listed in section 3.4.

**Teachability.** One wire per clause span; the clause type is a lexical function of the connective; output +5–8% tokens on real messages, ~0 on synthetic short rows. The sentence-split pilot (S1 91%→47% on dev because cross-sentence references are cut) shows the failure explicit links prevent.

**Validation.** `eval-clause-decomposition-v1`: the same 3.3k new compound rows printed flat (arm F) and chained (arm C), two SmolLM2-135M runs, judged on wild multi-clause proposition F1 (+0.08, CI excluding 0), long wire F1 and sealed non-inferiority. Owner decisions L1–L6 are in `questions.md`.

author: grammar-constrained-eval-agent
title: A GBNF grammar of the model surface generated from the live parser contract
body: tools/sop-gbnf.mjs emits a llama.cpp GBNF for the five model wires from SPEC, MODEL_TYPES, ROLE_NAMES and the enum exports (tests/sop-gbnf.test.mjs checks it with llama.cpp test-gbnf-validator); it follows the language automatically when the contracts change, and fails loudly when a SPEC field is neither ordered nor excluded. It accepts all 23,817 train, 5,131 dev, 5,033 test and 1,578 OOD golds, and 1,772 of the 1,885 wild accepted golds verbatim (the rest use another role or field order). Lesson from eval-grammar-constrained-v1: as a decoding constraint it must be parser-faithful; the canonical variant forbids strings with a leading blank that SmolLM2 emits as a separate token (about 10% of OOD outputs) and so rewrites valid outputs. Use --strings parser, and relax field and role order, when it is regenerated for the new language (clause links, $id, unparsed).

author: model-language-agent
title: SOP Lang: one clause per wire, conjunction link keywords, $id references and $q chains (L1-L4)
body:
Implemented in the one current language (no v1/v2 side by side; owner decisions L1-L4 of 2026-09-29 and the one-language decision):
- One finite clause is one short wire; a clause is never stuffed into a string.
- Subordination is a keyword line on the main clause pointing at the related clause: `because`, `so` (written on the effect clause), `if`, `unless`, `although`, `so_that`, `before`, `after`, `when`, `while`, each + `$id`. The set is one exported enum (`sop/enums.mjs` LINK_KEYWORDS) mapped to the types cause, condition, negative_condition, concession, purpose, before, after, during, so an experiment can swap the variant.
- A role value may be `$id` (a clause as an argument, or `$q`, the answers of an earlier query), at most one per wire.
- Host (L4): `if`/`unless` scopes the supposition to the query that names it; a timed before/after/when/while becomes until/from/during on the query; every other link is reported `not_checked` while the atoms execute; `$q` becomes a join; `$s` as an argument is not computable (queries) or reported (statements).
- Admission codes: link_form, link_too_many, link_duplicate, reference_multiple, link_reference_unknown, link_self_reference, link_target_type, link_condition_not_supposed, link_conflict, link_cycle, reference_unknown, reference_self, reference_target_type, reference_query_not_single.
- Choice left open by the proposal and decided here: link lines are wire-level only (not inside a match block); a link on a query qualifies the whole question.

author: linker-m0-agent
title: Linking M0/M1: one grammar, per-memory lexicon, linking report, baseline
body: The retired ontology grammar (config/ontology.sop, ONTOLOGY_SPEC, the concept wire, alias on predicates) is gone from tests, docs and wire help; predicate, lexeme and entity are knowledge wires (pages predicate/lexeme/entity, concept.html removed). Decisions by principle: (1) predicate_without_lexeme is reported only when the validator checks circuits for a base memory (validateProgram option linking, set by addKnowledge): an engine test world refers to predicates by id, so the smoke harness reports 0 warnings; the check is not silenced for memories. (2) New repeated_reading check replaces the Lexicon constructor throws. (3) POST /v1/memories takes imports, default [core-min], so no memory starts without a vocabulary. (4) The oracle ignores lexeme and entity wires. (5) rowWorld converts retired-grammar predicate blocks also when the generator hands them in memory. (6) The packet reports linking per bound mention (relation: lexeme/label/alias/id/description form, dictionary tier or copula reading with alternatives; entity: exact or accent-folded match and class). Baseline linking-v1 part 1 (2335 sealed test rows, mechanical labels): relation 100%, entity 99.9%, full query 100%, wrong-link 0%, a floor on the archive worlds the rows were generated with, not an open-vocabulary measure. Differential over 788 dev rows against the pre-M1 recording: 0 regressions against the expected results, 132 improvements (other agents' fixes since).

author: query-surface-agent
title: Query forms: what SymbolicLM writes for counts, superlatives, comparatives, ordinals, multi-hop and age (design before code)
body:
Probe on world-v1 (tools/eval/query-forms-probe.mjs, handwritten SOP through the product Agent) shows the RUNTIME already answers most forms; what is missing is the language-layer output, three small runtime gaps and measure vocabulary.
Forms and the SOP the rules should write (current DS021, no new keyword except rank position/top):
1 COUNT "How many countries border Germany?": mode count, select ?x, one match (rules v2.8 already do this).
2 SUPERLATIVE "the largest country in Europe", "the most populous city in Canada": ONE query: where all { match relation "be a" subject ?x object <class>; the restriction match (be in / be located in <scope>); match relation "be large" subject ?x object ?v } rank highest ?v. The adjective is a gradable attribute relation phrase (same shape the rules already use for "older than": relation "be old", role object ?v); lowest for small/young/short. Verified by hand on world-v1 with "area of": Russia.
3 ORDINAL "the second largest": the same query plus rank ... position 2 (WIRE CHANGE, see below); "the three largest": rank ... top 3.
4 COMPARATIVE yes/no "Is Canada larger than France?": mode exists, two value matches (?a, ?b) joined by compare ?a above ?b (the rules already write it for "older than"). "Which is bigger, Canada or Brazil?": select ?x, one value match, compare any {?x equal "Canada" / ?x equal "Brazil"} end, rank highest ?v (verified).
5 MULTI-HOP "Where was the director of Inception born?": two queries, @q1 asks the inner noun phrase (select ?d, match relation "direct" ... object "Inception"), @q uses role subject $q1. Works at runtime (verified on "the author of Hamlet", answer Stratford); the host answers each query and the final packet is the last. A relative clause "the country where X was born" is the same: @q1 select ?c where born_in X ?c, @q capital with object $q1. The rules must not keep the nested noun phrase as one string (convention C9 keeps only phrases that name one thing).
6 AGE "How old was X when she died?": the rules write the literal relation phrase "die at the age of" (subject X, object ?age), "How long did X live?" "live" with object ?years; the knowledge declares the derived measure: lived_years is a rule over born_on/died_on in world-v1 (compute), core-en gets lexemes "die at the age of", "live for", "be old when die". No stated event + when $s: that would make the language layer hold the semantics.
Measure vocabulary (knowledge, not language): core-en lexemes for gradable adjectives pointing to measure predicates ("be large/big" -> area_of, "be populous" -> population_of, "be tall" -> height_of). New file config/knowledge/core-en/0200-measures.sop to avoid colliding with linker-r2-agent's files; logged in the journal. Direction (older = earlier birth) needs a declared direction on the lexeme; not in this pass: "oldest/older" over people is reported as open.
Runtime gaps found: (a) rank had no position/top (add `rank highest ?v position 2`, `rank lowest ?v top 3`: position N = the rows with the N-th best distinct value, top N = rows among the N best distinct values; parser, lowering, js-reference, docs, tests); (b) the oracle's own sensitivity said a ranked select is monotone, so over an incomplete slice it returned a partial select instead of `incomplete` (R-P2 says a ranking is valid only over a complete slice): the oracle must mark rank non-monotone; (c) chat-turn lowering rejected a nested query whose shared variable has role classes country and place (Incompatible types for ?q1_0): inferVariableTypes needs class hierarchy compatibility (country is a place), via the lexicon.
Completeness guard: counts and rankings stay `incomplete` over unsettled slices (guard.mjs ranked already; oracle sensitivity fixed in (b)).
Evaluation: dev set eval-query-forms-v1 = world-v1 questions of these six forms with different words from the KBQA test rows (omp gpt-6-luna writes the questions and the intended SOP forms are not given to it; the answers come from the oracle on world-v1 through a reference SOP I author per template, not from the LLM). Sealed KBQA suites are measured once at the end (tag qf).

author: coding-agent-query-agent
title: codingAgentQuery design: the coding agent writes model-surface query wires, the shared path does the rest
body: Decision by principle (generic, one admission path): the coding agent writes the SAME model-surface output as SymbolicLM (query/constraint/unclear wires with relation phrases and quoted names, DS021), so admission, KnowledgeLinker, slice retrieval, StrategyRouter, oracle verification, completeness guard and rendering are shared and entity names are never in its prompt. It sees the memory vocabulary only (predicates with roles, labels, aliases, descriptions, classes, copula readings); an entity lookup is not given (55k entities; linking is the KnowledgeLinker's job). Implemented as a formalizer swap at Agent.turn (parser: coding_agent|local) with a validator (admission + only query/constraint/unclear/unparsed and supposed conditions), fix rounds via omp -c, fallback to local with reason, cache per (memory hash, model, message). unclear no_request from the agent falls back to local (statements, courtesy are local work).

author: coding-agent-query-agent
title: codingAgentQuery vocabulary by id from retrieved candidates (orchestrator design) and the output as a set of circuits
body: Implemented as decided: predicate ids from a closed candidate list (retrieval, not a dump), entity hints (ids only if listed), validator-enforced; missing vocabulary is the honest unclear kind relation_not_in_memory with the closest predicates and a gitignored gap log (chat_data/query-gaps.jsonl). Phrase mode is a measured arm (settings queryParser.mode). Output contract extensible: authorQuery returns circuits [{file, role, text}] (only role query today); phase 2 (definitions and labelled assumptions in the session layer) adds roles validated by the same call. Choices by principle: unclear kind added to the single reply table (DS021, wire help page) rather than a side channel; exact predicate id binds in linkRelation (an alias of another predicate cannot make it ambiguous); the full list is attached only as a file for omp (prefill cost for small local models).

author: coding-agent-query-agent
title: codingAgentQuery latency: no warm omp session; what keeps it low
body: Measured on world-v1 with openai-codex/gpt-6-luna: 9.5 s for one question alone (2 turns: write query.sop, finish), median 15.7 s and p90 23.3 s with three questions in parallel, 0.0014 USD nominal per question. Choice by principle: no continued omp session per chat session, because a continued session accumulates earlier requests (cost, cross-contamination of unrelated questions) while the large fixed part of the prompt (guide, 17.9k of 19.2k input tokens) is already served by the provider's prompt cache (cache_read). Identical requests on the same memory version are served from an in-process cache (no model call, cost 0). A lower-latency path for production is the completion backend against a local or hosted endpoint, which has no agent startup; calibration measures it.

author: omp-t1-author
title: T1 final owned verification and report

author: wire-type-reviewer
title: Metacognition on the logic book: what the existing wires express (P-1 review)
body: Executed over Agent.turn with fixed circuits and the js-reference oracle. Works on the product path: forced/possible/contradicted (supported/unknown/refuted per claim: logic:11, 121, 31, 91), which rule supports X (packet used/proof; the explain text omits the rule), would fact F make X derivable or block it (stated supposed + if $s; blocking through default except). Oracle only: why_not (missing base atoms; nothing when the gap is a rule), abduce over hypothesis wires, supposed proposed rules via if $r (diagnoses affirming the back / denying the front, logic:171, 181). Not expressible on the model surface: candidate rules (if names only stated; governance fields forbidden), per-option effect in one question, abduction over the message's options. Engine defect: abduce keeps explanations whose closure contradicts an admitted fact (logic:541 forced entry vs no tool marks; logic:501 grid failure vs lit neighbour). Proposal Q-LANG-10: query candidate $id + mode effect + abduce over candidates + if $rule; no new wire type.

author: query-candidates-agent
title: Q-LANG-10 implemented: candidates, mode effect, abduce over candidates
body: Q-LANG-10 option A (proposal P-1) is implemented exactly as approved, no new wire type. `candidate $id` on `query` (1-8, only `mode effect` and `mode abduce`) names a supposed `stated` wire or a session `rule`/`default` of the same output; it is in force only in that query's runs and never stored (the admission hands candidate and if-named session rules to the runtime as `approval proposed` wires outside the session layer). `mode effect`: the ground claim without candidates (baseline), then once per candidate; classes establishes (becomes supported), blocks (a decided claim becomes unknown: exception, strict contrary, absence), contradicts (becomes refuted or both), no_effect, inconsistent (a supposed fact whose contrary holds with it, or a fresh contradiction on an atom other than the claim; not counted). `abduce` over candidates: minimal consistent sets plus `necessary`. Validator codes: candidate_needs_mode, effect_needs_ground_claim, candidate_target, candidate_also_if, candidate_limit; the model surface adds candidate_temporal_link to enforce the stated rule that temporal links do not combine with candidates. Engines: oracle only; all wire engines refuse; R1 routes to the oracle. Logic book items as invented SOP programs: 171 (converse rule establishes), 91 (darkness no_effect), 541 (key story the only consistent one, necessary; forced entry inconsistent). Battery: 0 losses, 0 failures (full tier, 2492 L2 programs, 13 new candidate programs each with an irrelevant-facts variant, every engine 'n'). Open: the formalizer does not write these constructs yet; it needs a role-prompt extension (a fol-v3 successor of fol-v2) for argument questions, noted in P-1.
